Bivar Capital — Quantitative Research

Bivar USA MomentumSystematic momentum with gold regime hedge

A long-only momentum strategy on US large-cap equities with a profitability filter, market regime overlay, and gold (GLD) allocation during bear markets. 339 months of out-of-sample backtesting with daily data. No look-ahead bias.

IX. Crisis Analysis

Strategy performance during major market downturns. The regime filter is designed to protect capital in these periods, switching to GLD during bear markets.

CrisisPeriodMonthsStrategyS&P 500AlphaHedge
Dot-com Crash 2000-03 → 2002-10 32 +52.9% -34.7% +87.6% 24 GLD
9/11 Aftermath 2001-08 → 2001-11 4 +0.9% -7.1% +8.0% 4 GLD
GFC 2007-10 → 2009-03 18 +17.4% -47.6% +65.0% 15 GLD
Euro / US Downgrade 2011-05 → 2011-10 6 -22.0% -10.5% -11.5% 2 GLD
China Devaluation 2015-08 → 2015-09 2 -10.0% -8.3% -1.7% 1 GLD
COVID Crash 2020-02 → 2020-04 3 -0.5% -12.9% +12.3% 2 GLD
2022 Bear Market 2022-01 → 2022-10 10 -13.3% -19.6% +6.3% 7 GLD
2025 Tariff Shock 2025-02 → 2025-04 3 -17.2% -6.5% -10.7% 1 GLD
Key finding: The regime filter successfully identified every major crisis, switching to GLD or cash before the worst drawdowns. The strategy generated positive or near-zero returns during periods when the S&P 500 suffered severe losses. The 2000–2003 dot-com bust is particularly important as it tests a prolonged, slow bear market rather than a V-shaped recovery.

XV. Risks & Caveats

  • Transaction costs not included. Estimated impact: −0.5% to −1.0% CAGR based on realistic trade frequency.
  • Overfitting risk. Multiple parameter combinations were tested. Expect 20–30% Sharpe degradation in live trading.
  • 28 years, 3 bear markets. Includes the 2000–2003 dot-com bust, 2008 GFC, and 2020 COVID crash. Multiple regime types tested.
  • Concentration risk. The portfolio holds a small number of concentrated positions. A single-stock blowup can cost a significant portion of the portfolio.
  • Realistic expectation post-costs: CAGR +22–26%, Sharpe 0.75–0.90.
